transport: VE.Can — CAN bus on RJ45, NMEA 2000 based, Victron proprietary PGNs 0xEF00 addressable single frame / 0xFF00–0xFFFF broadcast single frame / 0x1EF00 addressable transport, priority 7, Victron NMEA 2000 manufacturer code 358. **No bit rate and no default node address for this model is stated in any committed document.** The VE.Can registers PDF does not give a bus speed at all.
gotchas: The register map almost certainly exists and the model binding does not. docs/victron-ve-can-registers-v20.pdf §1.10 "Battery Monitor settings" is plainly written for a device like this — 0x0FFE time-to-go (un16, minutes, read only), 0x0FFF state of charge (un16, 0.01 %, read/write), 0x1000 battery capacity (un16, Ah),

What is missing is one sentence naming the Lynx Shunt. The document names "Lynx Ion" for four specific messages, names a "BMV to NMEA2000 interface", and mentions the Lynx Shunt exactly once — as alarm bit 6, "Lynx Shunt not found", inside a Lynx Ion message. It never says the Lynx Shunt implements §1.10. docs/catalog/

0x0FFF state of charge is read/write. Writing it is a manual SoC synchronise, which is a real operation a rules engine would want and which has no CommandKind — the nearest existing verbs are `reset-counter` and `clear-fault` and neither means this. Recorded as a contract gap, not silently mapped.
unmappedReports: Channel 2 and channel 3 voltage / current / power, 0xED7D–0xED7F and 0xED6D–0xED6F — no MetricKind for a second or third DC channel. docs/catalog/can-bms.md predicted this would matter "the day a Lynx Shunt is catalogued"; this is that day., 0x1005 Peukert coefficient, 0x1004 charge efficiency, 0x1000 battery capacity — configuration a driver needs to interpret state-of-charge, with no contract slot. Not metrics, but not nothing either., 0x1008 / 0x1009 low state-of-charge set and clear thresholds — the device's own alarm setpoints. No slot.
